\begin{chapstatus}{The thread of this chapter}
Every rectangle drawn since Lecture 02 ended in a frame buffer that a controller sends to the screen many times a second. Next: the other devices: displays, keyboards, printers.
\par\medskip\textbf{Exit ticket} (two to four minutes, alone, on paper):
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=2em]
\item Why is a device never connected directly to the processor? Say what its controller does and how the processor talks to it.
\item A screen of 320 x 200 pixels uses 16 bits per pixel and is redrawn 30 times per second. How much frame-buffer memory is needed, and how many bytes per second must reach the screen?
\end{enumerate}
\end{chapstatus}
